Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording id: ff-20260305-ix3l9
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood Observability), Lena (Mariner Head of Platform), Omar (Mariner ML), Rachel (Mariner Security), Ben (Mariner Product)

Summary: quick telemetry readout from the pilot week, discuss tuning the canary thresholds and cutover decision gating, confirm runbook ownership and dry-run schedule.
Topics: telemetry anomalies, canary thresholds, rollout timing, fallback and rollback policies, KMS and audit log confirmation, pricing for burst/dedicated during cutover.

00:00 Lena: hey everyone, thank you for joining, I know we've got a packed agenda, um if we can keep to the 50 minute window that'd be great
00:12 Sofia: yep, thanks Lena. we'll go through the telemetry pack then decisions. Daniel and Ethan will cover the infra and alerts.
00:25 Daniel: quick note, apologies in advance for background noise, I am on the road. ok, so high level from Redwood's side, the pilot ran for seven days with the sample traffic you provided; we had two noticeable latency clusters on the 3rd day midday where 95th jumped from 420ms to about 820ms for long context requests.
00:48 Omar: yeah I saw that, i was replaying some logs, it looks correlated to a long tail of requests with 4k tokens, the KV cache warmed slowly, and our batching config hit the higher bin so throughput spiked.
01:10 Ethan: to add, our telemetry shows cache hit ratio fell from 87% to 54% in that window; we believe a model variant fallback happened — the router moved to a smaller quantized variant to preserve latency but the cold K V store rebuild cost increased token time.
01:34 Ben: when you say fallback, is that automatic? like it swapped models mid-request?
01:40 Daniel: not mid-request, but at the routing decision boundary; when node capacity crossed the soft threshold, policy called a compatible variant (we call it redwood-compact-v2) which has smaller KV memory footprint but worse Quality-of-Output in long-form generation. there were a handful of partial responses flagged by your eval harness.
02:05 Rachel: security question — during that event were any logs redacted or did PII flow into logs? we need assurance before go-live.
02:16 Priya: good call — we set retention to 30 days for pilot and PII redaction pipeline was enabled; Ethan can confirm sampling and redaction percentage.
02:26 Ethan: correct, sampling was at 10% for full transcripts; PII redaction ran with our regex/NER filter and we have audit traces in the log stream. no raw customer content was stored in plaintext K V cache; keys are ephemeral and masked.
02:45 Rachel: ok we still want to see the attestation docs, and the KMS key policy for the dedicated pool if we shift to reserved capacity during cutover.
02:55 Sofia: we'll attach the attestation snippets to the runbook we send after the call.
03:02 Lena: excellent. next on telemetry, canary thresholds — Ben and I want clear pass/fail gates, not fuzzy language. what are the concrete metrics?
03:14 Daniel: proposed gates: 95th latency not exceed 700ms for core routes, error rate < 0.5% rolling five minute window, quality degradation measured by eval set must be within 2% of baseline. if any gate trips, automatic failover to previous model version and manual review.
03:41 Ben: the 700ms 95th seems okay but our SLA target for customers is 500ms; how do we reconcile?
03:51 Sofia: for pilot go decision we set canary to a more conservative target that still protects user experience. during dedicated cutover we can enable burst capacity which should bring 95th closer to 500ms but that requires a short committed capacity window and higher cost.
04:12 Omar: can you quantify the cost delta for a 2-hour burst window during cutover? we need that in the runbook for finance.
04:20 Sofia: yes, i'll include a pricing delta table — rough numbers now: estimated extra cost for 2-hour dedicated burst is ~ $1.8K nominal for your traffic profile; i'll follow up with a more exact breakout.
04:34 Lena: ok add that as an action item.
04:40 Daniel: on monitoring and alerts, Ethan added two new hooks: model-switch detected and K V cache-warmup-failure. both post to your ops webhook and create a slack alert + PagerDuty if SLO breach exceeds 10 minutes.
05:00 Ben: good — we will want a mute window for test traffic so we don't generate unnecessary pages during the rehearsal.
05:07 Priya: we can configure a rehearsal mode where alerts are escalated to a separate test rotation. we'll note that in runbook step 2.
05:15 Omar: regarding A/B vs canary — we were leaning A/B to compare quality side-by-side, is that still recommended?
05:23 Daniel: both patterns work. A/B gives direct quality comparison at cost of traffic split complexity and routing weight management. Canary with staged traffic is simpler operationally. given your eval harness and user population, we recommend a hybrid: start with 2% A/B for quality checks, then move to 10% canary ramp for load validation, then full cutover.
05:49 Lena: timeline — we want go decision next Wednesday 03/11 after the dry-run on 03/10. is that feasible?
05:58 Sofia: yes, that's feasible. we should do the rehearsal on 03/10 with your on-call SREs and product.
06:05 Ben: one risk we found — the frontend retries on timeouts; if canary is slower it may cause duplicate calls and inflate traffic. can we add client-side retry headers to identify rehearsal traffic?
06:18 Daniel: yes, add X-Rehearsal-Id and we can route by header to ensure replay traffic is tagged. we'll also add a metric to filter those samples in analytics.
06:30 Omar: on the pilot results — overall accuracy on our eval set was within 1.6% of baseline on average, but certain long-form prompts had 6-7% delta which Ben flagged.
06:44 Ben: those spikes map to the subset of prompts that include multi-document summarization. sounds like a model variant quality issue, would prefer the canary to exclude those routes or send them to a pinned variant.
06:58 Daniel: we can create routing rules to send multi-doc summarization to pinned model (redwood-accurate-v1) during canary. it's a per-route override in the config. we'll add the override to runbook.
07:12 Rachel: legal needs to confirm data residency — some of these records are EU patient metadata, we need to ensure processing region is eu-west-1 for those requests. can your routing policy do region pinning by dataset?
07:25 Daniel: yes, we support region pinning and per-customer routing policy; for your EU dataset we can pin to eu-west-1 cluster. note that quantized variants available in eu-west may differ; we'll include model parity notes.
07:42 Lena: parity caveat is important, add to runbook and to the decision memo.
07:50 Priya: quick note on runbook structure — we'll provide sections: pre-cutover checks, rehearsal checklist, canary gating, rollback steps, communications matrix, cost table.
08:02 Sofia: i'll share the runbook doc and a lightweight slide deck after the call.
08:08 Omar: about the partial responses flagged earlier — can we see the sample transcripts and eval IDs so our ML team can triage?
08:18 Daniel: yes, we have the eval exports and will push a sanitized bundle to the shared drive (redwood-pilot/mariner/evals). note there are transcription errors in the export header occasionally, but the eval IDs map.
08:36 Ben: also add a smoke test for the fallback path, we want to verify that when the router falls back to a smaller variant we still meet basic functional correctness for critical flows.
08:48 Ethan: we'll add regression smoke cases and synthetic traffic that simulates high memory pressure. these will be part of the rehearsal run.
08:58 Rachel: on encryption at rest — you mentioned KMS. will keys be in our account or Redwood's?
09:06 Sofia: for dedicated/reserved pools during cutover we can use customer-managed KMS keys (your AWS account). we'll include key policy guidance in the security appendix.
09:20 Lena: good. any other major open risks?
09:24 Ben: scalability of the prefetch / cache warmup for cold-start sequences. we need a prewarming runbook step.
09:32 Daniel: agreed — we have a prewarm API call and a warmup plan: pre-populate KV cache for the top 1000 prefixes and run a 15 minute ramp before cutover. we'll show the sequence in the runbook.
09:47 Omar: will that prewarm generate production-like traffic that skews billing? ensure we mark it as rehearsal traffic.
09:55 Sofia: yep we'll mark with X-Rehearsal-Id and assign it to internal rehearsal budget.
10:05 Priya: recap next steps then?
10:08 Sofia: send runbook + pricing delta (action), attach security attestation + KMS notes, Daniel will update canary thresholds and add pinned-route for multi-doc summarization, Ethan to add test hooks, Omar and Lena to validate network/KMS, schedule 03/10 rehearsal.
10:30 Lena: thanks everyone, see you at rehearsal.

End of transcript.
